explain.say: Here is a puzzle. In space there is no air and no ground, yet a rocket can still speed up. What is it pushing against? The answer is Newton's third law, and you use it every time you take a step.

explain.say: Picture yourself on roller skates, pushing a wall. You push the wall forward. Now look at the arrow: the wall pushes you back, so you roll away. Forces always come in pairs. Which way do you roll?

Backwards, away from the wall, yes! A rocket does the same thing. It pushes hot gas down out of its engines, very hard. The gas pushes the rocket up just as hard. See the big up arrow? That is thrust, the push from the gas.

explain.say: The thrust, exactly! Great reasoning. Walking works the same way: your foot pushes the ground back, and the ground pushes you forward. Wow fact: India's LVM3 rocket, which launched Chandrayaan-3, lifts off with over ten million newtons of thrust. Try letting go of a blown-up balloon!

faq.q: How does a rocket push itself up?
faq.a: It pushes hot gas out of its engines downwards. By Newton's third law, the gas pushes the rocket upwards with an equal force called thrust.
asks: How does a rocket work in space?

faq.q: Why does the rocket need so much thrust?
faq.a: To lift off, the upward thrust must be bigger than the rocket's weight, and a full rocket weighs hundreds of tonnes.
asks: Why are rocket engines so powerful?

faq.a: When one object pushes on another, the second pushes back with a force of the same size in the opposite direction.
asks: every action has an equal and opposite reaction

faq.q: Why don't the paired forces cancel out?
faq.a: They act on two different objects. The gas pushes the rocket and the rocket pushes the gas, so each one moves.
asks: Why do action and reaction not cancel?

faq.q: How does walking use Newton's third law?
faq.a: Your foot pushes backwards on the ground, and the ground pushes you forwards with an equal force. On slippery ice that push is hard to make.
asks: How do we walk using forces?

facts: Newton's third law: forces come in equal and opposite pairs acting on different objects.
Chandrayaan-3 launched on an LVM3 rocket in July 2023 and landed near the Moon's south pole in August 2023.

quiz.say: You push on a wall with 50 N. How hard does the wall push on you?
quiz.show: You push on a wall with 50 N. How hard does the wall push on you?
quiz.why: The third-law pair is equal in size and opposite in direction.

wrong.0: Walls do push back: every force has a partner.
wrong.2: The partner force is equal in size, not double.

quiz.say: Air rushes backwards out of a balloon. Which way does the balloon move?
quiz.show: Air rushes backwards out of a balloon. Which way does the balloon move?
quiz.why: The balloon pushes air backwards, and the air pushes the balloon forwards.

wrong.0: The balloon pushes the air back, so the air pushes the balloon forwards.
wrong.1: The escaping air pushes back on the balloon, so it moves.
